subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should OpenClaw relax the default SSRF DNS-answer rule so mixed result sets can proceed after dropping blocked candidates, or keep the current any-blocked-answer fail-closed rule?
rationale: The root-cause patch is small, but it changes outbound SSRF policy for mixed DNS responses and should reflect maintainer security intent rather than an automated policy guess.

options.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
options.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and add all-blocked plus mixed-answer tests.

options.title: Keep any-blocked fail-closed
options.body: Treat polluted mixed DNS answers as intentionally blocked and document trusted proxy or fake-IP opt-in configuration as the supported workaround.

options.title: Make mixed-answer behavior opt-in
options.body: Preserve the current default and add or reuse an explicit operator-controlled policy for polluted DNS environments.

recommendation.title: Approve filtered mixed-answer semantics
recommendation.body: Allow the request only when at least one resolved address is allowed, pass only allowed addresses into the pinned dispatcher, and add all-blocked plus mixed-answer tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current SSRF assertion and recent net-policy history point to this person as the best available routing owner.
